description: Broad downstream-only research fixture. Each case provides synthetic but realistic evidence packets as if a strong web provider had already returned usable source material. The fixture tests whether later workflow stages can preserve, extract, and synthesize evidence without depending on live provider availability.

answer_key_policy.notes: Cases intentionally avoid ideal_response, expected_answer, golden_answer, and answer_key fields. The evidence packets are the fixed input; the final answer may use any natural format that is useful for the original prompt.

replay_contract.success_boundary: Downstream synthesis should turn the provided evidence into a coherent user-facing answer, or state an evidence gap when the evidence posture is insufficient.

cases.prompt: Research Crawl4AI, Firecrawl, Exa, Tavily, and Jina Reader for building an AI-readable web retrieval pipeline in 2026. Which parts are useful for a general research agent?

evidence_pack.title: AI-readable retrieval vendor docs comparison
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: Firecrawl is described as a crawl and extraction service that turns websites into markdown or structured output for agents. Tavily is positioned around search results with answer-oriented snippets. Exa emphasizes neural search over web content, while Jina Reader focuses on converting known URLs into LLM-readable text.
claim_hints: Firecrawl is strongest when the workflow already needs crawl and extraction.
Tavily and Exa are better discovery primitives than URL readers.

evidence_pack.title: Independent agent retrieval benchmark notes
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The benchmark separates discovery from materialization. Search-oriented tools returned broader candidate sets, crawler tools produced richer page text after a URL was known, and reader endpoints were most reliable as a low-cost normalization step. The report warns against treating a reader as a search index.
claim_hints: A general research agent should compose discovery, crawl, and reader steps.
Reader APIs cannot replace a high-quality search index.

evidence_pack.title: Open-source crawler implementation survey
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: Crawl4AI gives teams local control over browser and extraction behavior, which can help with custom sites and private deployments. The tradeoff is more responsibility for rate limits, rendering, retries, storage, and extraction heuristics than hosted APIs. It fits teams that want control over the retrieval lane itself.
claim_hints: Crawl4AI is useful when local control matters more than managed simplicity.
Hosted search APIs reduce operational burden but constrain customization.

cases.prompt: Research current options for scraping JavaScript-heavy sites for AI processing. Compare browser automation, hosted crawlers, reader APIs, and plain HTTP extraction.

evidence_pack.title: Rendering strategy field guide
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The guide recommends plain HTTP extraction for stable static pages, reader APIs for normalization of known pages, hosted crawlers for moderate JavaScript and extraction convenience, and browser automation for pages that require client-side state, navigation, or authenticated rendering. It emphasizes measuring each class separately.
claim_hints: Browser automation is the most capable rendering lane but also the most operationally complex.
Plain HTTP should remain the default when the page does not require JavaScript.

evidence_pack.title: Hosted crawler operations report
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: Hosted crawlers reduce setup time by bundling rendering, retries, and extraction, but they do not eliminate access failures. The report separates provider errors, rate limits, blocked rendering, and thin extraction so teams can identify whether the failure is discovery, fetch, or content parsing.
claim_hints: Hosted crawlers help with operations but still need gate-level diagnostics.
Anti-bot failures should be tracked separately from extraction failures.

evidence_pack.title: Reader API limitation memo
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: Reader APIs performed well on article-like pages and documentation pages after a relevant URL was selected. They failed to solve search, multi-step navigation, logged-in content, and pages where important content was created after user interaction. The memo frames readers as materializers rather than discovery engines.
claim_hints: Reader APIs are a downstream materialization primitive.
They cannot discover URLs or handle every interactive page.

cases.prompt: Research current observability options for agent workflows. Compare Langfuse, OpenTelemetry-based setups, Helicone, and Braintrust for traces, evaluation, and production debugging.

evidence_pack.title: Agent observability product documentation review
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: Langfuse documentation centers on LLM traces, prompt versions, datasets, scores, and evaluations. Helicone documentation focuses on proxying model calls, cost tracking, latency, request logs, caching, and gateway behavior. OpenTelemetry documentation is broader infrastructure tracing rather than agent-specific workflow evaluation.
claim_hints: Langfuse fits teams that need agent traces plus evaluation workflows.
Helicone is strongest around model request observability and gateway telemetry.

evidence_pack.title: Evaluation platform practitioner survey
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: Teams using Braintrust reported value from experiment tracking, eval datasets, and comparing model or prompt changes before release. The survey notes that evaluation tools are most useful when linked to real traces and failure examples, while pure logging tools rarely answer whether an agent got better.
claim_hints: Braintrust is more evaluation-centered than request-log-centered.
Eval tooling needs trace linkage to diagnose agent behavior.

evidence_pack.title: OpenTelemetry architecture note for agents
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The architecture note recommends OpenTelemetry when a team wants standard spans that integrate with existing infrastructure observability. It cautions that OpenTelemetry alone will not provide prompt datasets, human labels, LLM-specific scorecards, or agent regression analysis without additional product or custom layers.
claim_hints: OpenTelemetry is a foundation for traces, not a complete agent evaluation product.
A mature stack may combine OTel with LLM-specific eval tooling.

cases.prompt: What are some source-backed scientific breakthroughs or notable research milestones from April 2026? Separate confirmed findings from early or preliminary claims.

evidence_pack.title: April research journal highlights
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The journal roundup lists peer-reviewed April publications in materials science, climate modeling, and biomedical methods. It distinguishes replicated measurements and peer-reviewed experimental results from press-office claims. The strongest entries include clear methods, named journals, and independent expert context.
claim_hints: Confirmed milestones should be presented as peer-reviewed or method-backed findings.
Press-release-only claims should not be called breakthroughs.

evidence_pack.title: University research milestone tracker
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The tracker covers lab announcements, prototype demonstrations, and grant-funded milestones from April. Several are promising but early because they rely on small samples, animal models, prototype conditions, or unpublished datasets. The tracker recommends labeling them as notable developments rather than established breakthroughs.
claim_hints: Institutional announcements can identify leads but require cautious wording.
Prototype and animal-model results belong in a preliminary bucket.

evidence_pack.title: Science news verification checklist
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The checklist says a useful monthly science update should group claims by evidence maturity: peer-reviewed result, independent replication, preprint, conference presentation, prototype demo, or corporate announcement. It warns that novelty, funding size, and media attention are not substitutes for evidence strength.
claim_hints: The answer should separate evidence maturity levels.
Media attention alone is not enough to label a scientific breakthrough.

cases.prompt: Research current progress on perovskite-silicon tandem solar cells. What has improved, what is still a barrier, and what should a non-specialist believe?

evidence_pack.title: Tandem solar cell lab efficiency update
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: Recent lab reports show perovskite-silicon tandem cells continuing to reach higher conversion efficiencies than conventional silicon-only cells under controlled conditions. The evidence supports genuine technical progress in stacking absorbers, but lab-cell efficiency does not automatically imply low-cost mass manufacturing.
claim_hints: Efficiency progress is real in controlled lab settings.
Lab performance should not be translated directly into market readiness.

evidence_pack.title: Durability and degradation review
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The review identifies moisture, heat, ultraviolet exposure, ion migration, and long-term encapsulation as remaining durability barriers. It notes improvement in accelerated aging tests, but says field lifetime under commercial conditions remains the central proof point for non-specialists to watch.
claim_hints: Durability is still the main reason for cautious expectations.
Accelerated tests help but do not replace long field performance.

evidence_pack.title: Solar manufacturing scale-up memo
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The scale-up memo says the next hurdle is translating small-area, high-efficiency devices into repeatable production with acceptable yields, stable supply chains, and bankable warranties. It recommends describing the technology as promising and progressing, not as a finished replacement for mainstream silicon.
claim_hints: Manufacturing yield and warranty confidence are key commercialization barriers.
The practical answer should be optimistic but bounded.

cases.prompt: Research the current evidence on microplastics and human health. What appears reasonably supported, what is still unsettled, and what gets overstated in headlines?

evidence_pack.title: Human exposure review
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The review finds strong evidence that humans are exposed to microplastics through food, water, air, and consumer environments, and that particles have been detected in several human sample types. It treats exposure and detection as better supported than precise dose-response health outcomes.
claim_hints: Human exposure is reasonably supported.
Detection evidence is stronger than disease-causality evidence.

evidence_pack.title: Epidemiology evidence memo
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The memo says human epidemiology remains difficult because exposure measurement is inconsistent, confounders are hard to separate, and many mechanisms are inferred from animal or cell studies. It recommends saying possible risk is plausible but specific clinical claims remain unsettled.
claim_hints: Causal health claims remain unsettled.
Mechanistic plausibility should be separated from clinical certainty.

evidence_pack.title: Science communication audit
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The audit finds headlines often jump from particle detection to claims about specific disease outcomes without enough human evidence. It says the clearest public guidance is to reduce avoidable plastic exposure where practical while avoiding panic or unsupported claims about diagnosed harm.
claim_hints: The answer should warn against overstated disease claims.
Practical exposure reduction can be framed as precautionary.

cases.prompt: Research the current enterprise AI coding assistant market. Compare GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Sourcegraph Cody, JetBrains AI, and Amazon Q Developer for a 200-person engineering org.

evidence_pack.title: Enterprise coding assistant product docs
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: Copilot emphasizes GitHub and IDE integration with enterprise policy controls. JetBrains AI is strongest for teams already standardized on JetBrains IDEs. Amazon Q Developer fits AWS-heavy environments. Cursor offers a more agentic editor experience but may require governance review for large enterprises.
claim_hints: Recommendation should depend on existing developer environment.
Governance and admin controls matter for a 200-person org.

evidence_pack.title: Codebase context comparison
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The comparison says Sourcegraph Cody is differentiated by repository search and code intelligence context, especially where teams already use Sourcegraph. Cursor is praised for interactive editing and multi-file workflows. Copilot remains a default choice where rollout simplicity and broad developer familiarity matter.
claim_hints: Sourcegraph Cody is notable for codebase context.
Copilot is a safer default when rollout simplicity dominates.

evidence_pack.title: Procurement risk checklist
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The checklist advises testing data retention controls, seat management, supported IDEs, audit logging, repository indexing boundaries, and developer adoption friction before buying at scale. It recommends a pilot with representative repositories and measurable acceptance criteria rather than vendor demos alone.
claim_hints: A useful answer should recommend piloting with real repos.
Security and adoption criteria are as important as model features.

cases.prompt: Research EV charging infrastructure business models in the US in 2026. What models look viable, what risks matter, and what should a small property owner avoid?

evidence_pack.title: EV charging revenue model overview
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The overview identifies host-owned chargers, third-party operated chargers, fleet-focused depots, destination charging, and advertising or loyalty-supported charging as common models. It says utilization, electricity demand charges, maintenance, payment processing, and local incentives determine whether a site works.
claim_hints: Utilization is the central economic variable.
Different charging models fit different site types.

evidence_pack.title: Property owner deployment checklist
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The checklist warns small property owners not to buy hardware before confirming electrical capacity, permitting, utility rate structure, parking turnover, insurance, support contracts, and who handles uptime. It recommends starting with tenant or customer demand evidence rather than assuming chargers will attract traffic.
claim_hints: Small property owners should avoid hardware-first decisions.
Utility and maintenance details can break the business case.

evidence_pack.title: Charging station utilization study
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The study finds that profitable public charging depends heavily on location quality, dwell time, charger reliability, nearby amenities, and driver density. Low-use chargers can become a cost center even when incentives reduce installation cost, because fixed operating and maintenance burdens remain.
claim_hints: Incentives do not guarantee a viable site.
Reliability and location determine driver adoption.

cases.prompt: Compare current AI helpdesk platforms for a 100-person SaaS company. I care about Intercom, Zendesk AI, Freshworks, and Salesforce Service Cloud.

evidence_pack.title: Helpdesk AI product capability matrix
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: Intercom is framed around conversational support and AI-first customer interaction. Zendesk AI fits teams already using Zendesk ticketing and knowledge bases. Freshworks is positioned as a practical midmarket support suite. Salesforce Service Cloud is strongest where CRM data and enterprise workflows are already Salesforce-centered.
claim_hints: The best fit depends on the existing support and CRM stack.
Salesforce is powerful but may be heavier than a 100-person SaaS company needs.

evidence_pack.title: Customer support operations guide
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The guide says AI helpdesk value depends on clean help content, escalation rules, QA review, and measurement of resolution quality. It warns that weak knowledge bases cause bot deflection metrics to look good while customer satisfaction worsens. Human handoff design remains critical.
claim_hints: AI support platforms need knowledge-base readiness.
Automation should be judged by resolution quality, not deflection alone.

evidence_pack.title: SaaS buyer procurement notes
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: Buyers report that pricing, implementation services, CRM integration, analytics, and agent adoption often matter more than demo quality. For a 100-person SaaS company, the notes recommend choosing a tool that support managers can tune weekly without depending on a large IT program.
claim_hints: Operational tunability is a key selection criterion.
The answer should avoid recommending the heaviest platform by default.

cases.prompt: Research the current state of US state-level AI regulation in 2026. Which themes are emerging, which states are active, and what should a startup monitor?

evidence_pack.title: State AI legislation tracker
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The tracker shows state activity clustering around automated decision systems, consumer disclosure, public-sector procurement, deepfakes, child safety, and impact assessments. It identifies several states as active but warns that bill status changes quickly and startups should monitor enacted laws rather than headlines alone.
claim_hints: A useful answer should group themes rather than list every bill.
Bill status and enacted-law status must be kept separate.

evidence_pack.title: Startup compliance risk memo
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The memo says startups should monitor high-risk automated decisions, employment and housing use cases, health or finance claims, generative AI disclosure requirements, biometric data rules, and customer contract demands. It recommends mapping product use cases before tracking every state proposal.
claim_hints: Startup monitoring should start from product use cases.
High-risk decision domains deserve special attention.

evidence_pack.title: Public-sector AI procurement brief
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The brief notes that public-sector AI rules often focus on transparency, vendor documentation, data governance, human oversight, and impact review before agencies deploy AI systems. These requirements can affect startups indirectly when selling to governments or regulated enterprise customers.
claim_hints: Public procurement rules can shape vendor requirements.
Documentation and governance artifacts may become sales requirements.

cases.prompt: Research the EU AI Act implementation timeline and practical obligations for a small SaaS company that uses AI features but does not train foundation models.

evidence_pack.title: EU AI Act official timeline summary
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The timeline summary breaks obligations into phased application dates and emphasizes that duties depend on whether a company is a provider, deployer, importer, distributor, or user of a high-risk system. A SaaS company using third-party AI features may still have deployer obligations depending on use case.
claim_hints: Role classification matters more than company size alone.
The answer should avoid assuming a small SaaS company trains models.

evidence_pack.title: SaaS AI compliance checklist
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The checklist recommends inventorying AI features, mapping user-facing claims, identifying high-risk domains, documenting vendor model dependencies, preserving human oversight where needed, and preparing customer-facing transparency language. It treats the first step as product mapping, not legal conclusion shopping.
claim_hints: A practical answer should start with an AI feature inventory.
Vendor dependencies and user-facing claims must be documented.

evidence_pack.title: Legal commentary on foundation model distinction
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The commentary distinguishes general-purpose AI model provider obligations from downstream application obligations. It says companies that do not train foundation models should still check whether they substantially modify models, market AI systems under their own name, or deploy tools in regulated decision contexts.
claim_hints: Not training foundation models does not mean no obligations.
Substantial modification and high-risk deployment are important checks.

cases.prompt: Research the current US consumer privacy law landscape in 2026. Which state laws matter most for a mid-size internet business?

evidence_pack.title: State privacy law coverage map
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The coverage map shows that US privacy obligations are increasingly state-by-state, with larger states and states with active enforcement shaping practical compliance. It highlights rights to access, delete, correct, opt out of certain processing, and appeal decisions as recurring themes.
claim_hints: The answer should emphasize state-by-state compliance rather than a single federal rule.
Consumer rights themes recur across many state laws.

evidence_pack.title: Internet business privacy operations checklist
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The checklist says mid-size internet businesses should prioritize data inventory, privacy notice accuracy, request intake workflows, vendor data-processing terms, targeted advertising opt-outs, sensitive data handling, and records of consumer request responses before chasing every statutory nuance.
claim_hints: Operational readiness matters more than memorizing every statute.
Data inventory and consumer request workflows are core priorities.

evidence_pack.title: Privacy enforcement trend memo
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The enforcement memo finds regulators focus on misleading privacy notices, dark patterns in opt-out flows, children or teen data, sensitive health or location data, and vendor sharing practices. It recommends that companies validate what their product actually does against public claims.
claim_hints: Privacy claims should match actual product behavior.
Sensitive data and dark-pattern opt-outs are higher-risk areas.

cases.prompt: Research travel-friendly noise-canceling headphones in 2026 for calls, comfort, battery life, and reliability. Give me a practical shortlist, not marketing copy.

evidence_pack.title: Travel headphone lab comparison
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The lab comparison measures noise reduction, battery runtime, microphone clarity, comfort over long sessions, and case portability. It finds that top travel choices usually trade slightly bulkier designs for stronger ANC and longer battery life, while smaller models can be easier to pack but weaker on calls.
claim_hints: A shortlist should separate travel comfort from maximum ANC performance.
Call quality and battery life should be weighted explicitly.

evidence_pack.title: Frequent traveler durability survey
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The survey says hinge durability, pad replacement availability, Bluetooth reconnection reliability, multipoint behavior, and warranty support matter more to frequent travelers than small differences in codec marketing. Comfort complaints usually involve clamp force, heat, and ear-pad shape after two hours.
claim_hints: Reliability should include parts, warranty, and Bluetooth behavior.
Comfort needs long-session evidence, not just first impressions.

evidence_pack.title: Retail return pattern analysis
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: Return notes cluster around microphone disappointment, discomfort on glasses, app friction, and expectations that ANC blocks voices completely. The analysis recommends a practical shortlist with one best all-rounder, one call-focused option, and one comfort or budget alternative rather than a long ranked list.
claim_hints: A useful answer should avoid a long marketing-style list.
The shortlist should include fit and return-policy caveats.

cases.prompt: Research home battery backup options versus portable power stations for a homeowner who mainly wants outage resilience. What tradeoffs matter before buying?

evidence_pack.title: Residential backup power buyer guide
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The guide distinguishes whole-home or critical-load battery systems from portable power stations. Installed batteries can run selected circuits automatically and pair with solar, but cost more and require professional design. Portable stations are cheaper and flexible but usually require manual setup and support fewer loads.
claim_hints: Installed batteries are better for automatic critical-load backup.
Portable stations are better for budget and flexibility.

evidence_pack.title: Electrician installation checklist
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The checklist says homeowners should identify critical circuits, startup loads, panel compatibility, transfer equipment, permitting, battery placement, ventilation, and service capacity before buying. It warns against backfeeding unsafe connections or assuming a portable unit can power HVAC or large well pumps.
claim_hints: The answer should tell the user to map critical loads first.
Safety and transfer equipment are not optional details.

evidence_pack.title: Outage use-case comparison
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The comparison says short outages for phones, routers, fridge support, and medical devices can often be handled by portable stations or smaller critical-load systems. Multi-day resilience for heating, cooling, wells, or whole-home convenience usually requires a larger integrated system or generator hybrid.
claim_hints: Duration and critical loads should drive the recommendation.
Whole-home expectations change the cost category completely.

cases.prompt: Compare current cordless vacuum options for a small apartment with pets. I care about Dyson, Shark, Tineco, and Miele.

evidence_pack.title: Cordless vacuum pet hair lab test
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The lab test measures pickup on rugs, hard floors, edges, upholstery, and embedded pet hair. Dyson scores high on suction and tool ecosystem, Shark competes on value and flexible designs, Tineco offers smart features and wet-dry variants, and Miele emphasizes build quality but may cost more.
claim_hints: Pet hair performance should include rugs and upholstery.
Dyson is not the automatic value winner for small apartments.

evidence_pack.title: Apartment owner maintenance survey
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: Apartment owners care about storage footprint, dustbin emptying, hair-wrap resistance, filter washing, noise, and whether batteries remain useful after daily quick cleans. The survey says a smaller, easy-to-empty vacuum often beats a heavier flagship model in tight spaces.
claim_hints: Storage and dustbin behavior matter for small apartments.
Maintenance friction can outweigh raw suction.

evidence_pack.title: Retail reliability and replacement parts memo
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The service memo highlights battery replacement cost, brush-roll parts, warranty handling, and filter availability. It recommends comparing total ownership cost over several years, especially for pet owners who clean often and may wear out rollers or filters faster than occasional users.
claim_hints: The answer should include replacement parts and battery cost.
Pet owners need durability, not only first-month cleaning power.

cases.prompt: Research a 3-day Denver to Santa Fe spring road trip for someone who likes art, food, and easy hikes. Include realistic routing and seasonal caveats.

evidence_pack.title: Denver to Santa Fe route planning note
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The routing note treats the Denver to Santa Fe drive as a realistic full travel day with stops rather than a casual half-day. It suggests choosing either a mountain/scenic route with weather caveats or a faster interstate-heavy route, then saving Santa Fe time for galleries, food, and short walks.
claim_hints: The answer should not overpack the first driving day.
Route choice should mention weather and drive-time tradeoffs.

evidence_pack.title: Santa Fe spring visitor guide
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The visitor guide emphasizes the Plaza, Canyon Road galleries, Museum Hill, regional cuisine, and reservation-aware dining. Spring can bring pleasant days, chilly evenings, wind, and occasional late snow at higher elevations, so indoor art time should be balanced with flexible outdoor plans.
claim_hints: Santa Fe art and food should be the anchor after arrival.
Spring caveats should include chilly evenings and mountain weather.

evidence_pack.title: Easy hike safety and access notes
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: Trail notes favor short, lower-commitment hikes near Santa Fe or along the route, with attention to mud, snow patches, altitude, sun exposure, and road conditions. They recommend keeping hikes optional because spring conditions can change and the trip has only three days.
claim_hints: Easy hikes should be optional and weather-aware.
Altitude and spring trail conditions need caveats.

cases.prompt: Research family-friendly neighborhoods to stay in Chicago for museums, transit access, and walkability. Compare a few options and tradeoffs.

evidence_pack.title: Chicago family stay neighborhood guide
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The guide compares Loop/River North for central access, Lincoln Park for parks and family atmosphere, South Loop for museum proximity, and West Loop for restaurants with more transit tradeoffs. It warns that the best choice depends on whether museum access or neighborhood feel matters more.
claim_hints: A useful answer should compare neighborhoods by tradeoff.
South Loop is strong for museums while Lincoln Park is strong for family neighborhood feel.

evidence_pack.title: Transit access map notes
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: Transit notes favor staying near L lines or frequent bus routes if the family wants to avoid car logistics. Museum Campus is reachable but can involve walking gaps, stroller planning, weather exposure, and event traffic. Central neighborhoods reduce transfer friction for first-time visitors.
claim_hints: Transit proximity should be concrete, not generic.
Museum Campus logistics need walking and weather caveats.

evidence_pack.title: Family travel review synthesis
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: Family reviews emphasize predictable walking routes, quiet evenings, nearby breakfast options, room size, and easy returns to the hotel for breaks. The synthesis recommends avoiding a nightlife-first area if young children need early nights, even if restaurant access looks appealing.
claim_hints: Family comfort includes quiet evenings and easy breaks.
The answer should not optimize only for adult dining.

cases.prompt: Research the best neighborhoods to stay in Tokyo for a first-time 4-day visit focused on food, transit, and walkability.

evidence_pack.title: Tokyo first-time neighborhood comparison
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The comparison highlights Shinjuku for transit and energy, Ginza/Tokyo Station for polish and convenience, Ueno/Asakusa for older Tokyo atmosphere and value, and Shibuya/Ebisu for nightlife and food. It says a four-day first trip should minimize transfers and avoid chasing every district.
claim_hints: The answer should recommend bases, not a fantasy itinerary.
Transit convenience matters more on a four-day first visit.

evidence_pack.title: Tokyo transit planning primer
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The transit primer says station choice can matter as much as neighborhood name. Staying near a major line with straightforward airport access saves time, while very large stations can be confusing with luggage. Walkability should include station exits, hotel location, and late-night return routes.
claim_hints: Station location should be part of the recommendation.
Large stations are convenient but can be confusing.

evidence_pack.title: Food-focused Tokyo stay notes
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: Food notes say first-time visitors do well staying near dense casual dining, department-store food halls, ramen and izakaya streets, and easy breakfast options. The guide warns that famous dining districts can be crowded, so convenience and backup options often beat chasing one famous neighborhood.
claim_hints: Food access should include casual backup options.
The answer should balance destination dining with convenience.

cases.prompt: Research how the Works Progress Administration influenced American public art. Which programs mattered most, and what is the mainstream historical interpretation?

evidence_pack.title: Federal art programs overview
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The overview identifies New Deal arts programs such as the Federal Art Project and related mural, poster, community art, and teaching efforts as central to the WPA-era public art legacy. It emphasizes employment for artists and the creation of art in public buildings and community spaces.
claim_hints: The answer should name the major federal art programs.
Employment and public access were both central goals.

evidence_pack.title: Museum interpretation essay
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The essay says mainstream historians view WPA art as democratizing access to art, bringing modern and regional styles into public life, and legitimizing artists as workers. It also notes tensions over political symbolism, regional identity, federal patronage, and whose communities were represented.
claim_hints: The mainstream view is positive but not uncritical.
Representation and federal patronage tensions should be acknowledged.

evidence_pack.title: Public art legacy case study
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The case study follows murals, posters, and community art centers that remained visible long after the programs ended. It argues that the WPA shaped expectations that civic buildings, schools, libraries, and post offices could be sites of art rather than only administrative infrastructure.
claim_hints: The legacy includes changing expectations for civic spaces.
A good answer should connect programs to durable public art norms.

cases.prompt: Research interpretations of the Harlem Renaissance's political impact. Compare cultural, civil-rights, and critique-oriented readings without flattening them into one view.

evidence_pack.title: Harlem Renaissance cultural history survey
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The survey frames the Harlem Renaissance as a major expansion of Black literary, musical, theatrical, and visual expression that challenged racist stereotypes and created a more assertive public cultural identity. It treats cultural production as politically meaningful even when not organized as formal politics.
claim_hints: Cultural expression itself had political force.
The answer should not limit politics to legislation or parties.

evidence_pack.title: Civil-rights movement continuity essay
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The essay links Harlem Renaissance networks, publications, patronage, and public intellectual life to later civil-rights organizing and Black political consciousness. It avoids claiming a simple direct pipeline, instead describing a cultural and institutional foundation that later movements drew from.
claim_hints: The movement influenced later civil-rights politics indirectly.
A useful answer should avoid a simplistic cause-effect chain.

evidence_pack.title: Critical interpretation review
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: Critical readings emphasize class tensions, gender exclusions, dependence on white patrons, commercial constraints, and the gap between elite cultural visibility and material political power. These interpretations do not dismiss the Renaissance but complicate celebratory narratives.
claim_hints: Critical views should complicate, not erase, the movement's significance.
Class, gender, and patronage tensions matter.

cases.prompt: Research how historians explain the failure of Reconstruction in the United States. What causes get emphasized, and where do interpretations differ?

evidence_pack.title: Reconstruction historiography overview
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The overview says modern historians usually emphasize white supremacist violence, contested federal commitment, northern political fatigue, court decisions, economic conflict, and the withdrawal of military protection. It notes that older interpretations blaming Reconstruction governments are largely rejected.
claim_hints: Modern interpretations reject older blame-the-victims narratives.
Federal retreat and violence should be central.

evidence_pack.title: Violence and democracy case study
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The case study documents intimidation, paramilitary violence, election interference, and attacks on Black political participation as key mechanisms undermining Reconstruction governments. It argues that democratic collapse cannot be explained without the organized use of violence and the failure to suppress it.
claim_hints: Violence was not incidental; it was a mechanism of political reversal.
The answer should connect violence to democratic participation.

evidence_pack.title: Economic interpretation essay
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The essay highlights land, labor, debt, sharecropping, and northern capital as economic dimensions of Reconstruction's failure. It says historians differ on the weight of economic transformation versus political abandonment, but most connect both to the restoration of white elite power in the South.
claim_hints: Economic and political explanations should be integrated.
The answer should describe where historians differ in emphasis.

cases.prompt: Research current evidence and risks for GLP-1 medications in non-diabetic weight management. Summarize what a patient should discuss with a clinician.

evidence_pack.title: Clinical evidence review for GLP-1 weight management
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The review finds clinically meaningful weight loss in many non-diabetic adults using approved GLP-1 or related incretin medications, especially when combined with lifestyle support. It also notes weight regain can occur after stopping treatment, so patients should discuss long-term maintenance and cost.
claim_hints: Effectiveness is supported for appropriate patients.
Long-term maintenance and discontinuation matter.

evidence_pack.title: Safety and contraindication guidance
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: Guidance highlights gastrointestinal side effects, dose escalation, dehydration risk, gallbladder concerns, rare pancreatitis concerns, pregnancy planning, medication interactions, and history-based contraindications. It recommends clinician monitoring rather than self-directed use through informal supply channels.

A global update should include regional variety.

evidence_pack.title: Election outcome analysis memo
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The memo says election updates should distinguish changes in governing party, coalition math, mandate strength, voter turnout, and policy direction. A result can matter even when leadership stays in place if margins, alliances, or parliamentary balance shift.
claim_hints: Election impact includes coalition math, mandates, turnout, and policy direction.
No leadership change does not mean no political change.

evidence_pack.title: Election reporting uncertainty note
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The note recommends flagging provisional results, recounts, coalition negotiations, legal challenges, and delayed certification. It warns that early election summaries should separate confirmed outcomes from likely implications and analyst interpretations.
claim_hints: Election updates should separate confirmed results from implications.
Provisional results and coalition talks should be marked uncertain.

claim_hints: Apple, Google, and Meta face different antitrust theories.
A useful answer should separate app stores, search ads, and social platform issues.

evidence_pack.title: Amazon competition policy memo

claim_hints: Amazon antitrust pressure often focuses on marketplace conduct and seller treatment.
The answer should include business-model-specific risks.

evidence_pack.title: Antitrust uncertainty analysis
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The analysis warns that antitrust timelines are slow and outcomes depend on courts, settlements, agency priorities, and international regulators. It recommends separating filed cases, investigations, enacted rules, and speculative breakup or conduct-remedy predictions.
claim_hints: Tech antitrust outcomes are slow and uncertain.
The answer should distinguish cases, investigations, rules, and speculation.

cases.prompt: Give me an energy market update covering OPEC+, LNG, renewables, and grid interconnection bottlenecks.

evidence_pack.title: Oil market supply note
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The update says OPEC+ decisions remain important for oil supply expectations, but price movement also depends on demand forecasts, inventories, geopolitical risk, spare capacity, and compliance with announced production targets. A useful answer should avoid treating quotas as the whole market.
claim_hints: OPEC+ matters, but inventories and demand forecasts also shape oil prices.
Announced production targets are not the same as actual market balance.

evidence_pack.title: LNG and gas infrastructure memo
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The memo says LNG markets are shaped by export terminal capacity, shipping constraints, European and Asian demand, contract structure, and weather-sensitive gas consumption. It recommends distinguishing short-term spot volatility from long-term infrastructure and contract commitments.
claim_hints: LNG markets depend on terminals, shipping, demand, and contracts.
Gas market updates should separate spot volatility from infrastructure commitments.

evidence_pack.title: Renewables grid bottleneck report
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The report says renewable generation is expanding, but interconnection queues, transmission planning, permitting, storage integration, and grid upgrades can delay projects. The bottleneck is often not whether solar or wind can be built, but whether projects can connect and operate economically.
claim_hints: Grid interconnection and transmission are major renewable deployment bottlenecks.
Renewable growth should be discussed with storage and permitting constraints.

cases.prompt: Research current public health outbreak monitoring. Cover measles, dengue, avian influenza, and wastewater surveillance.

evidence_pack.title: Vaccine-preventable outbreak briefing
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The briefing says measles monitoring focuses on vaccination gaps, importations, school or community clusters, and rapid contact tracing because the virus is highly contagious. It recommends treating rising measles cases as a signal about under-immunized pockets, not only isolated travel events.
claim_hints: Measles outbreaks often reveal vaccination gaps.
Measles response depends on rapid tracing and community immunization context.

evidence_pack.title: Dengue and avian influenza surveillance memo
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The memo says dengue risk tracks mosquito distribution, climate, travel, and local control capacity, while avian influenza monitoring focuses on poultry outbreaks, wild birds, mammal spillovers, worker exposure, and genetic changes that might affect human risk.
claim_hints: Dengue monitoring is tied to mosquito ecology and local control.
Avian influenza monitoring tracks animals, workers, and genetic changes.

evidence_pack.title: Wastewater surveillance interpretation note
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The note says wastewater surveillance can provide early signals for pathogens such as respiratory viruses, but interpretation depends on sampling coverage, lab methods, sewage-shed population, reporting lag, and whether clinical testing confirms the signal.
claim_hints: Wastewater surveillance is useful but not self-interpreting.
A good outbreak update should distinguish signal, confirmed cases, and risk.

cases.prompt: Give me a space industry update covering Starship, Artemis, New Glenn, and Starliner.

Starship progress affects assumptions about lunar and launch economics.

claim_hints: Artemis schedule risk comes from multiple linked systems.
A useful update should explain dependencies, not only launch dates.

evidence_pack.title: Crew spacecraft reliability memo

Commercial crew value includes redundancy as well as individual spacecraft performance.

cases.prompt: Help me research wedding budget tradeoffs. Where should we spend or save across venue, guest count, catering, and photography?

Venue cost should be evaluated by what is included, such as tables, chairs, linens, coordinator time, and setup rules.
claim_hints: Guest count is usually the biggest wedding budget lever.
Venue prices should be compared by included services and restrictions.

evidence_pack.title: Catering cost tradeoff memo
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The memo says plated meals, open bars, late-night snacks, rentals, service fees, and staffing can move costs quickly. Couples can often save with a smaller guest list, limited bar, buffet or stations, seasonal menus, and fewer separate events.
claim_hints: Catering cost depends on service style, bar, rentals, and staffing.
Budget savings often come from guest count and event scope.

evidence_pack.title: Wedding photography value note
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The note says photography is often worth protecting if memories, family portraits, and documentation matter, but couples can adjust hours, second-shooter coverage, albums, and engagement sessions. It recommends evaluating portfolio consistency and backup process, not just price.
claim_hints: Photography budget can be adjusted by coverage hours and package extras.
Portfolio consistency and backup process matter more than lowest price.

cases.prompt: Research how to hire a home contractor safely. What should I check before signing a remodel contract?

evidence_pack.title: Contractor screening checklist
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The checklist says homeowners should verify contractor license status where applicable, liability insurance, workers' compensation coverage, bond requirements, complaint history, references, and whether subcontractors are covered. It recommends collecting proof directly rather than relying on verbal claims.
claim_hints: Contractor screening should verify license, insurance, and complaint history.
Proof should be collected before signing, not assumed.

evidence_pack.title: Remodel bid comparison guide
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The guide says bids should be compared by scope, materials, allowances, exclusions, timeline, cleanup, permits, change-order process, and payment schedule. The lowest bid may hide missing work, unrealistic allowances, or weak project management.
claim_hints: Remodel bids should be compared by scope, allowances, exclusions, and timeline.
The lowest bid can be risky if scope is incomplete.

evidence_pack.title: Home renovation contract memo
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The memo recommends a written contract with detailed scope, materials, permit responsibility, lien waiver process, milestones, payment caps, warranty terms, dispute process, and cancellation rights where available. It warns against large upfront cash payments without protections.
claim_hints: Remodel contracts should specify scope, payments, permits, warranties, and dispute process.
Large upfront cash payments increase homeowner risk.

cases.prompt: Research college savings options. Compare 529 plans, custodial brokerage accounts, Roth IRAs, and prepaid tuition plans.

claim_hints: 529 plans are education-specific and can offer tax advantages.
Custodial brokerage accounts are flexible but belong to the child.

evidence_pack.title: Roth IRA education funding memo

claim_hints: Roth IRAs are primarily retirement accounts, not dedicated college plans.
Using retirement savings for college has opportunity costs.

evidence_pack.title: Prepaid tuition and aid caveat note
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The note says prepaid tuition plans can reduce tuition inflation risk at participating schools but may be less flexible if the student attends elsewhere. Families should check state guarantees, eligible institutions, fees, ownership, and financial-aid treatment before choosing.
claim_hints: Prepaid tuition plans trade inflation protection for flexibility limits.
Families should check guarantees, eligibility, fees, and aid impact.

cases.prompt: Research a practical moving checklist. What should be handled first for utilities, address changes, insurance, and school records?

Moving plans should start with dates, access, and essential logistics.

evidence_pack.title: Address and records update checklist

School records and enrollment requirements should be handled before moving when possible.

evidence_pack.title: Insurance during move memo

claim_hints: Moving can affect renters, homeowners, auto, and health insurance.
Coverage effective dates and belongings-in-transit protection should be checked.

cases.prompt: Research a personal privacy cleanup plan. Prioritize password manager, MFA, data broker opt-outs, and credit freezes.

evidence_pack.title: Personal security priority guide
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The guide says the highest-impact first steps are using a reputable password manager, creating unique passwords, enabling multi-factor authentication on email, banking, cloud storage, and social accounts, and securing account recovery methods. Email security is especially important because it resets other accounts.
claim_hints: Password manager plus MFA is the first personal privacy/security priority.
Email account security should be treated as a root account.

evidence_pack.title: Identity theft prevention memo
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The memo says credit freezes at the major credit bureaus are a strong low-cost control against new-account fraud, but they do not stop existing-account takeover or every form of identity misuse. People should store freeze PINs and know how to thaw credit before applying for loans.
claim_hints: Credit freezes help prevent new-account fraud.
Credit freezes do not replace account security or fraud monitoring.

evidence_pack.title: Data broker opt-out operations note
evidence_pack.relevant_extract: The note says data broker opt-outs can reduce exposed personal information but are labor-intensive and may need periodic repetition. It recommends starting with high-visibility people-search sites, removing old public posts, tightening social profiles, and using MFA before spending heavily on opt-out services.
claim_hints: Data broker opt-outs help but require repetition and do not fix account security.
A practical cleanup plan should prioritize password manager, MFA, freezes, then opt-outs.
